tldr: Sony Music and Warner are suing Anthropic over alleged use of tens of thousands of copyrighted works, raising another significant legal and training-data risk for model providers.
AWS has open-sourced Kiro Crew, a workspace for running asynchronous coding agents across tasks such as incident investigation, migrations, and pull-request monitoring.
Nvidia's data-centre advantage is increasingly shifting from GPUs alone toward networking and traffic-control systems that improve utilisation.

top.title: Sony Music and Warner sue Anthropic over training-data piracy
top.summary: Sony Music and Warner Chappell have sued Anthropic in the US, seeking damages over alleged use of tens of thousands of copyrighted works, with potential penalties of up to $150,000 per work and $25,000 per instance of stripped copyright information.
top.why: Treat training-data provenance and copyright controls as a model-provider risk: this case could affect which models are acceptable for production and how vendors price legal protection.

top.title: Nvidia's AI advantage is expanding from GPUs to networking
top.summary: The latest generation of data-centre systems is improving AI efficiency through smarter traffic control and networking, rather than relying only on additional processor cycles.
top.why: When sizing large inference or training clusters, evaluate the network fabric and traffic-management stack as part of performance and cost—not just GPU count.

top.title: AWS open-sources Kiro Crew for asynchronous coding agents
top.summary: AWS has announced Kiro Crew, an open-source workspace for running multiple Kiro coding agents across sessions, tools, and tasks, including incident investigation, ticket triage, migrations, and pull-request monitoring without continuous supervision.
top.why: This is worth evaluating as an alternative to manually orchestrated coding-agent jobs, but require approval gates, isolated credentials, and audit logs before allowing it to change production systems.

also.title: Runplane targets the risk of unsupervised AI trading agents
also.summary: The project was built after an AI agent misread a risk signal and moved $1.2 million in trades, positioning it as a response to the need for stronger controls around autonomous actions.

also.title: AgentGate adds signed receipts for AI-agent SaaS actions
also.summary: This early Show HN project records AI-agent SaaS actions with signed receipts, aiming to provide verifiable evidence of what an agent did.

also.title: AI-generated commits are outpacing code-verification capacity
also.summary: The report says GitHub commits have doubled in four months while the capacity to review and verify that code has not kept pace.
